findings.summary: The MT12 derivation `grep -oE '^\s*"[a-z][a-z-]*",'` requires a TRAILING COMMA, so a module declared as the last entry without one -- legal Kotlin, and the usual way a list is written -- is dropped from ALL. That is MT12's own failure mode with a narrower trigger: the delta path filters candidate module dirs through ALL, so the module is silently skipped while the success line prints a count. The usage header two lines up still hardcodes "all eight", the fourth copy of a fact the derivation just removed three of.
findings.failure_scenario:
Ran the script's exact grep over `include(
 "format",
 "plugin"
)`: output is `format` only. So `settings.gradle.kts` gaining `"wal"` as the final entry without a trailing comma, plus `wal/` in the diff, yields MODULES empty -> `ok no module changed`; `GATE_SCOPE=full` prints `ok 8 module(s) checked` over nine modules; and `scripts/check-module.sh wal` fails with `unknown module: wal`, the same split-brain MT12 named. Fix is one character class: `'^\s*"[a-z][a-z-]*",?\s*$'`, and make the header say "every module" rather than "all eight".
